text:
Semyon Varlamov's six starts this season are a comeback story first. A knee injury in late 2024 cost him the rest of that season and all of last, and his opening-week start against the Rangers was his first NHL start in about two years. At 38, nobody would have blamed him for stopping.

He has been better than his .898 save percentage suggests. He has saved 5.6 goals more than the shots he faced usually allow (goals saved above expected), in the 94th percentile per 60 among goalies, with a 2-2-1 record. The reason is the hard chances: he is .846 on high-danger shots against a league .685, stealing nearly seven goals on 45 of them.

The odd part is in the middle. He is only .792 on medium-danger shots against a league .863, which is where most of his goals against have come from. Six starts is a tiny sample for any goalie, and both numbers will move.

For the Islanders, a reliable backup behind Ilya Sorokin matters. So far, Varlamov has given them that.
